title: Loops
description:
## Loops in Assembly
There's no `while` or `for` keyword in assembly. Loops are just labels + compare + jump back.

```asm
    mov rcx, 5        ; counter
loop_start:
    ; do something
    dec rcx            ; counter--
    cmp rcx, 0
    jg loop_start      ; if counter > 0, jump back
```
That's a while loop. `dec` subtracts 1, `cmp` checks if we're done, `jg` jumps back if not.


---
## Assignment:
LHINX needs to print a boot countdown. Print `Booting...` 3 times using a loop. Use `rcx` as your counter. (check the hint.)
starterCode:
section .data
    msg db "Booting...", 10
    len equ $ - msg

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    mov rcx, 3
    ; write your loop here

    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Remember: `syscall` destroys `rcx` and `r11`. You'll need to save `rcx` before the syscall and restore it after. You just learned how to do that...
